text:
pagerduty-bot: PAGER: Incident 2026-03-mgpu-004 triggered — high error rate observed on /v1/generate in hosted-prod. Symptoms: multi-GPU communicator disconnects, container restarts on node gpu-ephemeral-17. Paging oncall SRE.

Alice: Oncall (Alice) — ack. Looking now. Which jobs and models impacted?

Bob: I see repeated NCCL errors in pod inference-xyz-0 logs: 
```
[2026-03-17T14:12:05Z] NCCL WARN Communication error, exiting
[2026-03-17T14:12:06Z] Xid 79, GPU reset detected
[2026-03-17T14:12:06Z] Aborting process: connection to rank 2 lost
```
Looks like a communicator signal loss followed by container respawn.

infra-bot: k8s events: pod inference-xyz-0 OOMKilled 3x, lastRestartCount=3, Node gpu-ephemeral-17 reported GPU driver reset at 14:12:06.

Carol: Copy. Suggest cordon/drain gpu-ephemeral-17 and move running TP jobs off it. Also check nvlink health and PCI errors on that host.

Bob: Running `kubectl get pods -o wide --field-selector spec.nodeName=gpu-ephemeral-17` -> there are 4 inference pods and 2 training ephemeral jobs. Initiating graceful drain for canary inference pods only.

Alice: Customer impact: Dave, can you confirm request failure rate?

Dave: Dashboards show /v1/generate 5xx spike to 9% and 95th latency climbed to ~2.3s for 12:00-14:15 UTC. Only hosted-canary and hosted-prod routes affected; dedicated customers unaffected. Link: https://grafana/redwood/boards/abc (internal)

Siva: Quick mitigation: enable NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1 and NCCL_IB_TIMEOUT=200 on canary tasks to avoid hard abort while we drain. Will patch deployment env and restart pods.

Bob: Applying env patch to canary deployment now: 
```
kubectl set env deploy/inference-canary NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1 NCCL_IB_TIMEOUT=200 -n hosted
kubectl rollout restart deploy/inference-canary -n hosted
```
Patch applied, restarting 2/2 replicas.

Carol: Cordoned gpu-ephemeral-17 and started drain for non-critical jobs. Kept one replica to collect logs, will copy dmesg and nvidia-smi output for infra team.

Alice: Good. We should also temporarily reduce pipeline parallel world size for canary to avoid multi-GPU collectives on marginal nodes. Can we roll a quick config?

Bob: Updating canary config to TP=2 (was 4) and restarting. This reduces cross-node collectives.

infra-bot: Collected logs -> dmesg shows multiple ECC and PCIe AER errors around 14:11:58; driver reports GPU reset. Attaching snippet to ticket.

Dave: Customer-facing note: small percentage of requests failed with 503. Will draft status update once we stabilize.

Alice: Handoff in 15m to Carol (next oncall). If we still see driver resets after drain, escalate to hardware team and consider node reprovision and full host swap. Add post-incident: investigate kernel/driver upgrade and node-level nvlink stress test.

pagerduty-bot: On-call handoff scheduled: Alice -> Carol at 14:30 UTC. Incident status: mitigation in progress; canary patched, affected node cordoned.

Carol: Taking over. I'll follow up on hardware ticket and confirm rollback plan if driver resets continue. Logging action items in INC-2026-004.
